verdict.reasoning: Transcript: "I've been feeling kind of under the weather for the past four days. It started with a sore throat..." and "it was quite painful to swallow... For one of the days." This supports a 4‑day history of sore throat, initially with painful swallowing.
Transcript: "runny nose" and later "it's clear, but sort of getting my nose stuffed all the time. It's very hard to get it free." This describes clear discharge and congestion.

Transcript: "and it sort of... It's sort of going into a cough now" and later "that started recently, like just maybe yesterday. And it's dry for now." This supports a dry cough since about yesterday.

Transcript: "I forgot to mention that I'm also having night sweats... And this is again been going on for last three, four days. Has it? Doctor: Yeah. Yes." Duration given is 3–4 days, not specifically the past 2 days.
Transcript: "Any headaches at all?" – "Yeah, yeah, that's still there... Just sort of general. And they're not always there, but... they would come and go." No timeframe of "past 2 days" is stated.
Transcript: "any general muscle pain or aches? Joint pain?" – "Yeah, yeah, That's. That's sort of started in the past couple days." This matches muscle aches over the past 2 days.
Transcript: "Kind of bad and tired." and also "Makes me a bit tired." This supports reported tiredness.

Transcript: "I had some fever in the beginning, but it's now sort of going down. I've been taking some paracetamol and I Bupren for that and they help." This matches an initial fever resolving with paracetamol and ibuprofen.

Transcript: "no pain in the chest, but... I feel a bit winded on exertion... When you say winded, do you feel more short of breath... mainly on exercise, but when you're resting, there's no problem?" – "Yeah, yeah, When I'm resting, it's okay." This supports mild exertional shortness of breath.
Transcript: "In terms of your chest, otherwise, have you any difficulty breathing or any pain in your chest?" – "So no pain in the chest..." This is a denial of chest pain.
Transcript: "Any pain in your ears at all?" – "No." and "You don't feel blocked or any discharge coming out of your ears?" – "I don't think so." This supports denial of ear symptoms.
Transcript: "any feeling of nausea or any vomiting?" – "None of that." This is a clear denial of nausea and vomiting.
Transcript: "Tell me about your bowels. Are your bowels working okay?" – "Yeah, yeah, I think so." and "Passing urine okay?" – "Yeah, yeah." This supports normal bowel and urinary function.

Transcript: "How's your appetite, sir?" – "Yeah, I've been drinking a little bit more... other than that, okay." and "You're eating okay, otherwise?" – "Maybe a bit less than what I would usually have." This indicates slightly reduced appetite.
Transcript: "Yeah, I've been drinking a little bit more. More than the usual..." This supports increased fluid intake.

Transcript: "Are you otherwise fitting well or do you have any other medical problems... ?" – "So otherwise that I'm fine. There's. There isn't anything that I'm taking or I'm being treated for?" This indicates no known past medical problems.
Transcript: "There isn't anything that I'm taking or I'm being treated for?" This supports that he is on no regular medications (acute paracetamol/ibuprofen are symptomatic, not chronic).
Transcript: "Any allergies at all to any medications. I should be aware Of, No." This supports no known allergies.
Transcript: "Yeah, my grandma has diabetes." and "Do you know what type of diabetes it is?" – "I think it's type two." This matches grandmother with type 2 diabetes.
Transcript: "I think one of my great granddads had an eczema." This supports great‑grandfather had eczema.
Transcript: "Tell me, who do you live with at home?" – "I live alone."
Transcript: "And you said you're working at the moment, is that right?" – "Yeah, yeah." "What do you do for work?" – "I'm an accountant."
Transcript: "in terms of smoking, do you smoke at all?" – "Yeah, occasionally. No cigars and things on company parties." This is occasional smoking.
Transcript: "And what about alcohol?" – "Occasionally, I would have some. I'm not a very big drinker." – "Again, socially, with work." This supports social alcohol use.
Transcript summary: "I think you probably have... a bit of a viral... illness, and maybe a viral upper respiratory tract infection or maybe early signs of a flu." This matches the stated assessment.

Transcript: mild exertional dyspnea described ("I feel a bit winded on exertion... when you're resting, there's no problem?" – "Yeah, yeah") and assessment only mentions viral URTI/early flu with no mention of LRTI; absence of LRTI signs is a direct inference from the assessment and history.

Transcript includes night sweats ("I'm also having night sweats"), muscle aches ("any general muscle pain... ?" – "Yeah, yeah, That's. That's sort of started in the past couple days."), and intermittent headaches ("they're not always there... they would come and go"). These are associated symptoms.

Transcript: "things you can do... get plenty of rest... pushing fluids and make yourself well hydrated, continuing with the regular paracetamol and ibuprofen." This is supportive care with rest, hydration, and paracetamol/ibuprofen.
Transcript: "I'll probably advise you taking a day or two of work if you can" and patient: "I think I'll take a couple of days off." This matches advice to take 1–2 days off work.

Transcript: "If next week you're still better, I want you to come back and see me." and safety netting: "If you're really not getting better, if you have a high fever or your breathing is becoming a bit more labored, or chest pain, I'd like you to come back and see me much sooner." This aligns with monitoring symptoms and returning if fever persists, SOB worsens, chest pain develops, or no improvement after about a week.
Transcript is entirely history and advice; there is no documentation of any physical examination findings. Stating none are documented matches the transcript.
